title: Terminal stream receive capacity verification
verification_method: Focused final-size and retention tests, complete partitioned Release regression tests, permanent BenchmarkDotNet rows, alternating source-backed ProtocolLab runs, and independent review.
scope: Verify that newly buffered STREAM data reaching a validated final size rents exact capacity without changing final-size validation, flow control, delivery order, completion, pooling ownership, or nonterminal coalescing behavior.
preconditions: Final-size and flow-control validation complete before receive-buffer mutation.
Nonterminal STREAM data retains the existing 4 KiB initial and 8 KiB continuation coalescing policy.
Existing buffered segments are not copied merely to compact capacity when a later FIN establishes final size.
evidence: Partitioned complete Release suite: 9,579 passed and 5 intentionally skipped in the main partition; the two suite-order-sensitive tests passed 5/5 independently.
procedure: Receive data-bearing FIN frames and confirm retained capacity equals payload length while unread-byte accounting remains exact.
Receive a FIN-only frame before terminal non-FIN data and confirm final-size-aware capacity, exact delivery, completion, and release.
Confirm nonterminal data retains coalescing capacity and a 1 KiB terminal continuation tail does not reserve an unused 8 KiB block.
Run focused receive, read lifecycle, shard ownership, and metrics tests.
Run the complete Release test inventory using a deterministic partition for the two known suite-order-sensitive tests.
Compare exact-baseline and candidate BenchmarkDotNet rows and five alternating source-backed raw QUIC c64/s100 pairs.
expected_result: Terminal receive capacity is exact whenever final size is known, nonterminal coalescing and QUIC behavior remain unchanged, ownership balances, and repeated raw QUIC evidence shows no end-to-end regression.
status_summary: Passed. Focused tests passed 51/51. The complete Release inventory passed as a deterministic partition: 9,579 tests passed with five intentional skips in the main partition, and the HTTP/3 incomplete-content close and dropped-server-FIN recovery tests each passed 5/5 independently after both showed suite-order timing failures in all-in-one runs. Independent review found and drove fixes for FIN-first reordered data and a below-threshold continuation-tail proof. Matched local ShortRun timing was noisy and did not establish a microbenchmark speed claim. Five alternating source-backed c64/s100 raw QUIC pairs all passed with zero failed or timed-out requests; candidate median throughput was 63.63 MB/s versus 56.16 MB/s and median p95 latency was 5,591.06 ms versus 6,159.57 ms. One additional baseline warmup timed out and remains retained negative evidence. All performance evidence is local shared-host and non-publishable.
